sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Harrisburg, PA?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Harrisburg means working in a state capital where most homes are rented, prices are modest and many sellers are landlords or heirs. The Census Bureau counts 50,522 residents as of July 1, 2025 and 22,137 households for 2020 to 2024.

Only 36.6 percent of occupied homes in Harrisburg are owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $124,200, median gross rent is $1,062 and median household income is $48,099, with 30.5 percent of residents in poverty. About one adult in four, 25.9 percent, holds a bachelor's degree.

Those figures shape a sale. Buyers are often investors who price a house by what it will rent for, and lenders can be cautious on a property that needs work. A seller with a vacant or tenant-occupied Harrisburg house may do better with a buyer who purchases as-is.

sections.h2: Where is Harrisburg and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Harrisburg sits on the east bank of the Susquehanna River and is the seat of Dauphin County and the capital of Pennsylvania. The city covers 8.1 square miles of land and 3.3 square miles of water, which makes it the third smallest U.S. state capital by land area.

  • Paxton Creek empties into the Susquehanna inside the city, and the river forms the line between Dauphin and Cumberland counties.
  • Downtown holds the State Capitol complex, and there are more than a dozen neighborhoods and historic districts around it.
  • Six municipal historic districts, several national historic districts and architectural conservation overlays guide new work in older blocks.

Be careful with addresses. Several nearby townships, including Lower Paxton and Middle Paxton, use Harrisburg as their mailing name even though they sit outside city limits and follow their own codes. Check whether your parcel is inside the city before you read any rule below.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for a Harrisburg house sale?
sections.html:
Government jobs keep the Harrisburg market steady even when prices are low. The Region Economic Development Corporation lists the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania as the area's largest employer at 21,885 people, followed by the federal government with about 18,000. Health care, Giant Food Stores, the Hershey companies and TE Connectivity round out the top ten regional employers.

The city's history explains its housing stock. The Pennsylvania Canal and then the Pennsylvania Railroad made Harrisburg one of the more industrial cities in the Northeast in the 1800s, and the population fell by nearly half between 1950 and 2000. Many blocks therefore hold older rowhouses and brick twins that need updates. The annual Pennsylvania Farm Show, held in Harrisburg each January since 1917, brings visitors every winter.

sections.h2: Which roads and transit connect Harrisburg homes to the region?
sections.html:
Interstate 83 runs through the middle of the city and meets Interstate 81 to the north. Interstate 76, the Pennsylvania Turnpike, passes south of town, and Interstate 283 links the turnpike and I-83 southeast of the city. U.S. 22 crosses the northern part of the city, and Route 230 follows Cameron Street.

Harrisburg International Airport sits southeast of the city in Middletown and serves about 1.2 million travelers a year. Capital Area Transit runs local bus service, and the city also has rail and intercity bus connections. Mean travel time to work for Harrisburg residents is 20.1 minutes.

sections.h2: What permits and codes apply to repairs in Harrisburg?
sections.html:
The city's Bureau of Codes handles building permits, trade licenses, rental registration and property complaints, and you can reach it at 717-255-6553. Harrisburg follows the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, with the 2021 international code editions in force from January 1, 2026.

  • Permits are required for roofing, fences, sheds, decks, replacement windows and doors, any structural work, new furnaces and any work above $1,000.
  • Residential permit applications must be decided within 15 business days, or 5 days if stamped by a licensed design professional. Historic Review Board review adds time.
  • A building permit expires after 6 months if work is not continuous.
  • Electricians and plumbers must hold a city license, and every contractor needs a city business privilege license.
  • The Bureau Health Officer enforces lead-based paint hazard rules for residential structures.

If you did work in the past without a permit, call the Bureau before you list. That way you know what is open on the property before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What must a buyer do with a Harrisburg rental or condemned house?
sections.html:
A buyer of a Harrisburg rental or condemned house takes on city deadlines the day the deed is recorded. The Bureau of Codes says a non-condemned rental must be registered within 10 days of purchase, and a condemned property needs permits to lift the condemnation within 30 days of purchase.

The program under Ordinance 1-2017 also requires an inspection at least once every five years, taxes and utilities to be current before a unit can be rented, and a local managing agent when the owner lives more than 50 miles away. The annual landlord license is separate and runs through the Bureau of Licensing, Taxation and Central Support at 717-255-6513.

If you sell a tenant-occupied house, tell the buyer which of these items are paid up.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work when you sell in Dauphin County?
sections.html:
The Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds records the deed and collects transfer tax. Pennsylvania imposes 1 percent on the value of the real estate, and counties also collect a local share for school districts and municipalities. Both buyer and seller are jointly liable for the tax, so ask your title company to show how the closing statement splits it.

Property that passes by will or intestate succession is exempt from the transfer tax when the heirs receive it. A later sale by the heirs is a separate transfer. The Department of Revenue's valuation factor for Dauphin County is 2.61 for documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

The Recorder of Deeds calculators note that a deed for nominal consideration between tax-exempt parties carries no transfer tax, and checks are payable to the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Harrisburg house?
sections.html:
Most Harrisburg sellers choose among three paths.

  • An agent listing suits a house in good condition and a seller who can wait for a lender-approved buyer.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts the listing fee, but you handle showings, forms and negotiation yourself.
  • A cash offer fits a vacant, damaged, inherited or tenant-occupied property, and you set the closing date.

Compare the net amount after repairs, carrying costs and fees on each, not only the offer price.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Harrisburg house with tenants still living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes over the lease, and a buyer who plans to rent must register the unit with the Bureau of Codes within 10 days of purchase. Give the buyer your lease, deposit details and proof the rental fees are paid.

faqs.q: What if my Harrisburg house has been condemned?
faqs.a: You can still sell it. The Bureau of Codes says a buyer must secure permits to lift the condemnation within 30 days of purchase, so cash buyers who handle repairs are the usual fit for these properties.

faqs.q: Do I pay transfer tax on an inherited Harrisburg house?
faqs.a: Not when the house passes to you by will or intestate succession, since the Department of Revenue lists those transfers as exempt. When you later sell to a buyer, the sale carries the 1 percent state tax plus the local share.

faqs.q: Who do I call about permits on a Harrisburg house I want to sell?
faqs.a: Call the Bureau of Codes at 717-255-6553. It processes permits and inspections, and the city lists roofing, windows, decks, sheds and work above $1,000 among the jobs that need one.

faqs.q: Is my address inside Harrisburg city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Lower Paxton, Middle Paxton and other nearby townships use a Harrisburg mailing address but are separate municipalities with their own codes. Check your tax bill or the Dauphin County parcel record to confirm which municipality bills you.
